reason: The text describes the Israelites' escape from Egyptian slavery and divine deliverance at the Red Sea (Exodus 14), not a fight for national sovereignty over land. The Hebrews are fleeing, not actively fighting. When they see Egyptian chariots pursuing them, Moses explicitly tells them: 'The Lord will fight for you; you need only be still' (וַיְהוָה יִלָּחֵם לָכֶם וְאַתֶּם תַּחֲרִישׁוּן). God—not the Hebrews—wages war against Egypt, parting the sea and destroying the Egyptian army. The passage emphasizes the Israelites as witnesses to divine salvation rather than as active combatants. Furthermore, this passage marks the beginning of the Exodus journey; they have not yet entered or fought for the promised land.
